clue.text: Not delivering straight down the wicket

definitions.text: Not delivering straight down the wicket

parts.words: Not delivering straight down the wicket
parts.note: in cricket a bowler who makes the ball turn sharply off the pitch sends it on a deviating line rather than a straight one

explanation.surface: A cricket coach complains that a bowler keeps straying off line.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the bowler delivers the ball down the pitch (the wicket) at the batsman; a slow bowler who makes it turn is deliberately not bowling straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow bowling that makes the ball turn after bouncing deliberately avoids a straight line to the batsman.

parts.note: not what a pig eats, as the surface suggests, but the pig itself served up as meat

explanation.surface: A label on a bucket of farmyard swill.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the twist: the food is the animal, not its feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of the pig is what we eat at table, so the animal turned into food bears this name.

parts.note: ST, short for street, a kind of way
rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an odd remedy offered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or patent cure-all is a kind of medicine, often of dubious worth.

clue.text: Composer alternatively with very loud music

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A composer's work is played either very loudly or not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff, the German who wrote Carmina Burana, is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Rock song for the very young

definitions.text: Rock song for the very young

parts.words: Rock song for the very young
parts.note: rock suggests rock music, but here it means rocking a cradle while singing a baby to sleep

explanation.surface: A rock band records a track aimed at small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' wants to be the music genre; it is the gentle swaying that sends a baby to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing song sung while rocking an infant to sleep is a cradle song for babies.

clue.text: One turned left at present time

indicators.note: turned means the letters of one are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Someone turned left at the present moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges ONE as NOE. 'present time' is the season of gifts, not 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season of giving gifts, so it is fairly called a present time.

clue.text: Having an enjoyable time on record?

definitions.text: Having an enjoyable time on record?

parts.words: Having an enjoyable time on record?
parts.note: a phrase for enjoying oneself, read literally as sitting in the spiral track cut into a vinyl disc

explanation.surface: Someone is having a great time, and it has been documented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on record' suggests officially documented; the question mark points to a gramophone record's track.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means performing well and enjoying it, while literally a stylus sits in a vinyl record's track.

parts.note: cocky means arrogant, but read as like a cockerel it pictures the bird's comb drooping

explanation.surface: Someone who was arrogant has been taken down a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockerel's comb (its crest) drooping is the picture behind the word for dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humbled and dejected has lost their swagger, pictured as a cockerel whose comb has dropped.

clue.text: Yelling, pity it's a shocking thing

parts.note: yelling is crying out loud
as in 'what a shame', a pity

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that a dreadful event is a real pity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something deplorable, a real outrage or disgrace.

clue.text: Fundamentals that are both lousy and abrasive

parts.note: lousy literally means infested with lice, and so full of their eggs, nits
abrasive means rough like sand or grit

explanation.surface: Basic principles that are both rotten and harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' looks like 'bad', but it is literal: infested with lice and nits.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the basic practical details means dealing with the essentials of a matter.

clue.text: It lets you know there's a rough time ahead

definitions.text: It lets you know there's a rough time ahead

parts.words: It lets you know there's a rough time ahead
parts.note: seems to mean a personal warning of hard times, but read literally it is a weather warning of rough seas

explanation.surface: Something warns that hard times are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: A rough time sounds like personal trouble; literally it is bad weather, warned of by a flag or cone hoisted at coastal stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal warning flag or light alerts shipping to a coming gale, a rough spell of weather.

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A police informer's name is written on a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: A NARK is British slang for a police informer; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a police spy or grass who informs on others is known by this word.

clue.text: It is designed to raise one's standing in hotel perhaps

definitions.text: It is designed to raise one's standing in hotel perhaps

parts.words: It is designed to raise one's standing in hotel perhaps
parts.note: raising one's standing sounds like boosting reputation, but it means carrying a standing person up between floors

explanation.surface: Something meant to improve your status, maybe in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' suggests status; it is literally standing in the car that carries guests between floors.
explanation.definitionFit: The British word for an elevator carries standing passengers up between the floors of a building.

clue.text: But it is not the work of a locksmith

definitions.text: But it is not the work of a locksmith

parts.words: But it is not the work of a locksmith
parts.note: locks here are tresses of hair, so trimming them is a barber's job, not a key cutter's

explanation.surface: A remark that some job was not done by a locksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locksmith' makes you think of door locks; the locks are on someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber trims locks of hair, which is a joke on the craftsman who works on door locks.

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word at is turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at being jeered when a thing is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AT into TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by custom or social rule is off limits.

parts.note: a punter is a gambler, one who bets

explanation.surface: A gambler lends a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punter' is British for someone who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who encourages or assists, often in wrongdoing, gives support to another.

clue.text: Language coming from Thailand boat first

indicators.note: first says the boat word is placed ahead of the Thailand letter

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth
T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A dialect spoken first on a Thai boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon or slang peculiar to a group is a kind of private language.

clue.text: Lady accepting resistance to tie the knot

indicators.note: accepting means the woman's name takes in another letter

parts.note: Mary is a lady's name
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A lady overcomes her reluctance to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts R inside MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie the knot is an idiom for getting wed.

clue.text: Joke by one in senile dotage

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone makes a joke beside an old person in their dotage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being doddery and confused in old age is described by this informal word.

parts.note: eg, for example, means 'say'
one's is I'S, I for one plus 's

explanation.surface: Someone, for instance, is getting shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: EGIS is the American spelling of aegis, a shield or sponsorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the aegis of someone means under their shield or sponsorship.

indicators.note: contains means the gift word holds another letter within it

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of radioactive

explanation.surface: A present holds the first radioactive element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts R (first of 'radioactive') inside BOON. The surface implies the element is radioactive; boron is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, atomic number 5.

parts.note: a Blue is awarded for representing Oxford or Cambridge at sport, and a cap for playing for one's country
a Blue is awarded for representing Oxford or Cambridge at sport, and a cap for playing for one's country

explanation.surface: A wing player wins two sporting awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a wing player; it is a bird, the bluecap being a name for the blue tit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluecap is a dialect name for the blue tit, a bird, so a creature with wings.

parts.note: endless suggests a train of infinite length, but it is one that runs without halting at stations

explanation.surface: A train that goes on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' means without stops, not without length.
explanation.definitionFit: An express service running without halts never pauses, so its journey is unbroken.

indicators.note: return means the word to is read backwards

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: An actor returns to Shakespeare to say hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moor of Venice is the title character of one of Shakespeare's tragedies.

definitions.meaning: hooting car horns make this noise

explanation.walkthrough: TOOTING is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Car horns honking make this noise, and the same word names a neighbourhood in south London.

parts.note: VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Virginia politician has to make things up as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: To vamp is to improvise a simple accompaniment in music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, to vamp is to extemporise a simple accompaniment.

indicators.note: unceasingly, read as without its ending, cuts off the final letter of the word for worked

parts.note: plied means worked, as in plied a trade

explanation.surface: A dancer worked tirelessly at a ballet step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unceasingly' trims the D from PLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plié is a ballet step in which the dancer bends the knees.

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mixed doubles match served up with a bit of root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: An eddo is the edible corm of the taro plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The eddo is the starchy underground stem of taro, eaten as a vegetable.

definitions.meaning: a small container for warming liquids over a spirit flame
the volcano on the east coast of Sicily

explanation.walkthrough: An etna is a small spirit-burning vessel for heating liquids, named after the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit lamp heater carries the name, and Sicily's active volcano erupts regularly.

clue.text: Certain variety act somehow deleted in Ireland

indicators.note: variety says the letters of certain are rearranged
somehow deleted says the letters of act, in any order, are taken away

explanation.surface: A certain variety act was mysteriously cut from a show in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' shuffles CERTAIN; 'somehow deleted' takes out A, C and T, leaving E, R, I, N. Erin is a poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is a poetic old name for the Irish nation.

indicators.note: confuses means the letters of your dialect are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says that your accent muddles explanations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something explanatory throws light on a matter, making it plain.

parts.note: to keep something is not to sell it
a company is a business

explanation.surface: A judge advises not to sell the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo, as a couple do when seeing each other regularly.
